crane.text: A common crane, taller than you'd think, unfolds a wing, bugles once across the reeds, and goes back to ignoring you.

broads_boater.text: We hired a cruiser for the week. Day one we hit a bridge. Day two, a swan hit us. Day three we've moored up at the pub and we're not moving.

broads_peat.text: The sides of the broads are steep, straight walls under the water, with ridges of peat between. Joyce Lambert spotted that from her borings in the 1950s. Lakes don't make straight walls. People with spades do.
Around the 1300s the sea level rose and the diggings flooded. The medieval peat-cutters basically made a national park by accident.
